_comment: Ratchet baselines for scripts/verify.py. Lowering a number is routine (run --update-baseline after a cleanup). Raising one is a deliberate regression and must be justified in review.
_note: updated 2026-09-02: sidebar_links 25 -> 27 is a CORRECTED MEASUREMENT, not link growth — audit F-11 changed the admin-zone predicate from is_platform_admin (which the check's stub evaluated falsy, hiding the zone: platform_admin measured 16) to user.is_admin() (what @admin_required enforces); an Administrator platform_admin now renders 27, within SIDEBAR_LINK_BUDGET 28. No link definitions were added. shell_conformance 3 remains.
_note2: updated 2026-09-17: evidence_contract 29 -> 30 for merge 424162db (PR #20, fix/model-class-deduplication). The substantive commit (9cfe2af6) carries real same-commit test coverage (tests/test_fast_init_model_tenancy.py, tests/test_outcome_tenancy.py -- 33 passed, 0 failed, red-then-green demonstrated per commit body) but used a prose 'Regression:' line instead of the literal 'Evidence:' keyword the gate scans for, and the merge commit itself (424162db) carries no trailer of its own. Rewriting already-pushed main history to fix the wording was judged not worth a force-push; accepted as one unit of debt rather than silently ignored. Future commits on this bucket's pattern should use a literal 'Evidence:' trailer to avoid tripping this gate.
_note3: updated 2026-09-20: sidebar_links 27 -> 28 is real link growth, not a corrected measurement. The Ask page has one front door, "Ask a question", first in every persona's My work, so platform_admin (the worst case) renders one more. The Twin map has no link of its own and is reached from the Ask page. SIDEBAR_LINK_BUDGET moves 30 -> 31 with it.
_note4: updated 2026-09-21: an Impact Analysis My-work link (fix/t104-impact-sidebar) was added for solution_architect and business_architect, matching enterprise_architect's existing one. business_architect now also measures 28, tying platform_admin rather than trailing it -- _note3's "platform_admin (the worst case)" no longer names the only worst case. sidebar_links stays 28 (no ratchet change); this note only corrects which role(s) that number describes.
_note5: added 2026-09-22: public_repo_hygiene_record_ids (1728) registered by hand, measured directly against this tree rather than via --update-baseline (which re-measures every ratchet and was not run, to avoid shifting unrelated numbers in this change). Large because the checked shape (a review-record-id token, or the word "orchestrator") collides with this codebase's own permanent conventions -- see scripts/check_public_repo_hygiene.py's own docstring for the full measurement and reasoning. The pre-existing hits were not fixed in this change; they are frozen debt the ratchet now prevents from growing.
_note6: updated 2026-09-22: public_repo_hygiene_commit_messages removed as a ratchet key. A full-history count of commit messages cannot stay green: GitHub's squash merge appends its own Co-authored-by: trailers to the merge commit after every gate has already run on the pull request, so three ordinary multi-author merges already put the full-history count at 1034 against a baseline of 1031 on origin/main, before this change even lands. The gate now checks only the commits under review (origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF..HEAD in a pull request, origin/main..HEAD otherwise) at zero tolerance -- no baseline number describes a moving range, so there is nothing to register here.
_note7: updated 2026-09-22: public_repo_hygiene_record_ids 1728 -> 416. The content scan now reads only comments, docstrings and string literals (not executable code), the record-id pattern is restricted to the four letters the process actually uses, a bare id counts only next to a role word, a round mention or "finding", and a small set of business-reference-number prefixes and product-vocabulary phrases are excluded by construction. The remaining 416 is real, pre-existing content this change did not remove: the standalone word "orchestrator" as ordinary product vocabulary beyond the specific phrases now allowlisted, and existing review-process references already committed before this change, in both source comments and docstrings. Frozen debt, same as before; the ratchet only prevents it from growing.
_note8: updated 2026-09-22: public_repo_hygiene_record_ids 416 -> 659. Three of the allowlist prefixes (a task-reference, a finding-reference and a deliverable-reference prefix) turned out to be broad enough to also exclude this codebase's own task and readiness-finding references, which share the exact letter-and-digit shape the rule exists to catch; removed. Two narrower, genuinely product-only entries (an exact deliverable-code prefix and its own review-id-letter collision) replaced part of what was removed. The rise is a correct, more accurate measurement of already-present content, not new content -- the previous 416 undercounted by exactly the amount the three broad prefixes were hiding.
_note9: updated 2026-09-22: public_repo_hygiene_record_ids 659 -> 668. An f-string's own literal text was never reaching the scan at all (it tokenises as FSTRING_MIDDLE on this codebase's interpreter, not as a STRING token); now included, and 9 pre-existing hits inside f-string literals are counted for the first time. Real, previously-invisible content, not new content.
_note10: updated 2026-09-22: public_repo_hygiene_record_ids 668 -> 676. The HTML/Jinja narrowing only ever read `<!-- -->`/`{# #}` comments, so an inline <script> body's own `//`/`/* */` comments and a template's visible text (the literal text a browser renders between tags) were both unreachable. Now scanned -- a <script> body with the same rules as a .js file, and visible text with everything else (tags, attributes, `{{ }}`/`{% %}` code, <script>/<style> blocks, comments already covered separately) blanked out first. 8 pre-existing hits, real and previously-invisible, counted for the first time.
_note11: updated 2026-09-23: public_repo_hygiene_record_ids re-measured at 676, unchanged, after two further fixes to the same scan: the DEL- deliverable-code allowlist context check gained a left word boundary (a longer word merely ending the same way was previously misread as the prefix and wrongly excused; no such case exists in the current tree, so the count does not move), and title=/alt=/placeholder=/aria-label= attribute values are now read with the visible-text rule rather than discarded along with their tag (none of the four attributes carries a record-id- or role-word-shaped value in the current tree either). Both fixes proven against synthetic probes, not against a change in this number. The remaining 676 still carries the same frozen debt described in _note7 through _note10; the time-unit shape ("T-1 day"-style bare ids still matching the record-id pattern) is accepted as part of that same debt, not remeasured against.
_note12: updated 2026-09-25: two new shared Library links ("Canvases", "Frameworks") were added for every role. sidebar_links stays 28 -- business_architect and platform_admin (zero headroom) each lost one same-page duplicate link, and enterprise_architect (one link of headroom) lost "Duplicate Detection", moved to portfolio_manager's My work (ample headroom there); it stays in a sidebar zone, just not enterprise_architect's. See app/utils/role_access.py's SIDEBAR_LINK_BUDGET and per-role comments for detail. No ratchet or budget change.
_note13: updated 2026-09-26: untenanted_reads 2990 -> 2988. Two request-supplied/stored user ids (an ARB audit action's acting-user lookup, an ADM audit event's actor lookup) that used to resolve with a bare db.session.get(User, ...)/User.query.get(...) now go through app.utils.tenant_users.user_in_org, which the gate does not flag as unfenced.
_note14: updated 2026-09-26: untenanted_reads 2988 -> 2788. VendorOrganization (200 reads) is the shared vendor catalogue, deliberately not tenant-scoped (ADR-0003, see its docstring), so it is now listed in GLOBAL_MODELS in scripts/check_untenanted_reads.py with that reason instead of being counted as an unfenced read.
_note15: updated 2026-09-26: untenanted_reads 2788 -> 2633. APQCProcess (97) and TechnicalCapability (58) are shared reference catalogues (rows created only by seed commands; the tenant link for APQC is SolutionAPQCProcess), now listed in GLOBAL_MODELS in scripts/check_untenanted_reads.py with the evidence. FeatureFlag and ElementTemplate were checked and deliberately left counted.
_note16: updated 2026-09-26: store_agreement 1 -> 4 is a measurement step, not a regression. The gate now asks every store and screen for work packages, gaps (split by gap_kind: every row / capability shortfall / plateau transition), risks, application owners, architecture decisions, three pending-proposal queues (AI change approvals, review queue items, relationship suggestions, each its own question), applications with a recorded annual cost, contracts and vendors, and its screens sign in through the session registry instead of answering 401. Surfaces answering a different question are not registered (live-computed capability-map gaps and RoadmapGap, ComplianceGap, TechnologyRoadmapInitiative, DecisionLedger). Measured on the demonstration organisation (flask seed-demo-company), four genuine disagreements, each attributed to the branch that closes it: capabilities (the existing one; feat/r1-one-capability-store), work packages (UnifiedWorkPackage 12 vs every list screen 0; feat/r1-one-work-package-store), application owners (ApplicationOwner 20 vs ApplicationOwnership 0 and owner text 0; feat/r1-one-owner-record) and applications with a recorded annual cost (application cost columns 20 vs ApplicationCost 0; feat/r1-one-application-cost). Gaps no longer disagree once each surface is compared with surfaces showing the same gap kinds. Each consolidation lowers this again. A fresh database with no organisation measures 0.
_note17: added 2026-09-28: tenant_isolation_route_coverage_pct 44.0 is the share of identifier-bearing routes (one rule, one method) proven to refuse another organisation's identifiers, measured by the route sweep in tests/test_tenant_isolation_matrix.py and enforced by that test, not by a verify.py gate. It is the one ratchet here where HIGHER is better: raise it after proving more routes, never lower it.
_note18: updated 2026-10-04: sidebar_links 28 -> 30 is real link growth, not a corrected measurement. Two new My-work links ("Model as of", "Changes") were added for enterprise_architect, the role that owns the capability model and audits its evolution. enterprise_architect was already the worst case at 28 (tied with business_architect); it now measures 30, still within SIDEBAR_LINK_BUDGET 31. No other role's links changed.
_note19: updated 2026-10-05: merged origin/main, which carries PR #353's Approval Inbox link and moves SIDEBAR_LINK_BUDGET 31 -> 32 (see app/utils/role_access.py's comment) — this branch's own _note11 cited the now-stale 31. Re-ran scripts/check_sidebar_links.py after the merge: sidebar_links stays 30, enterprise_architect still the worst case. The count is unchanged because Approval Inbox is permission-gated (requires="general") and the script's stub user never satisfies a requires= guard (the same stub-evaluates-falsy limitation this file's 2026-09-02 note recorded for the admin-zone predicate), so the new link adds nothing to what this ratchet measures, for any role. The two links _note11 describes ("Model as of", "Changes") are the only ones behind the 30; only the budget figure needed correcting, to 32.
_note20: added 2026-10-10: background_mechanisms_thread_instances 29 is a NEW measurement, not growth. The register is now keyed on file, kind and enclosing function, so the gate counts thread instances (29) beside the files holding them (background_mechanisms_thread, still 22); the older key counted one entry per file and could not see a second pool in a listed file. Both may only fall.
